prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Dallas. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can definitely help — I can either (A) pull up a short, targeted list of specific Dallas-area practices with phone numbers and short reasons to call (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood), or (B) give immediate guidance you can use right now to find and phone the best implant doctors yourself. Which would you prefer?

If you want me to look up specific offices, tell me:
- Your ZIP code or the Dallas neighborhood you’re closest to
- Any preferences: oral surgeon vs periodontist vs prosthodontist, price/insurance concerns, sedation options, same-day/All‑on‑4 interest, or a short timeframe

If you prefer to start calling right away, here’s a concise plan + script and what to look for:

Who to call first (best order)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeon — best for surgical complexity, bone grafting, general anesthesia.
- Board-certified periodontist — specialists in implants and gum/bone health; good for routine to complex implants.
- Prosthodontist — if you need the restorative/final tooth work (crowns, bridges, full-arch rehabilitation).
- Multidisciplinary implant centers — convenient if they coordinate surgery + restoration in-house.

What to ask on the phone (quick script)
- “Do you place dental implants? How many do you place per year?”
- “Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging for treatment planning?”
- “Which implant brands do you place (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.)?”
- “Do you do bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed? Do you do sedation or general anesthesia?”
- “Do you restore implants in-house, or will a different dentist do the crown?”
- “What is an estimated range for a single implant with crown, and do you offer payment plans?”
- “Do you have before/after photos or patient testimonials I can review?”
- “Are you board-certified? Can I verify that on your website?”

What to prioritize in answers
- Experience (number of implants/year, specific experience with cases like yours)
- Use of CBCT and digital planning (reduces surprises)
- Clear plan for restoration (not every surgeon restores the crown)
- Implant brands and warranty/guarantee policy
- Financing/insurance and transparent estimates
- Good patient reviews and before/after photos
- Board certification (ABOMS for oral surgeons, ABP for periodontists, ABO for prosthodontists)

Red flags
- Vague answers about experience or implant brand
- No CBCT for planning complex cases
- No clear restorative plan (who does the crown)
- Extremely low price with no explanation

If you want, give me your ZIP code/neighborhood and any preferences and I’ll put together 4–6 specific Dallas practices to call, with phone numbers and why each would suit your needs.
